The factor $2^{2b+4}$ cancels the $2^{-b-2}$ carried by each stored operand, and the inverse image under $\Phi$ is the original integer coefficient convolution

Digit $a_j$ is stored with numerator $a_j2^{p-b-2}$ in a signed real word followed by a zero imaginary word, representing $a_j2^{-b-2}$, so the inputs have norm below $1/4$; $S-q$ zero records pad each array.
Apply $\Phi$ to obtain arrays $u,v$ of exact $p$-bit values (here $u,v$ are the scaled digit arrays, not the integers).
Multiply corresponding coefficients exactly and truncate toward zero to $p$ fractional bits, obtaining $z$.
Compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)$ and multiply by $S$, obtaining $\widetilde w$.
Multiply by $2^{2b+4}S$, round to the nearest integers, write each as a signed $(3b+1)$-bit word, and apply $\Phi^{-1}$ removing the padding.
Propagate radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order and output exactly $2n$ bits.
The exact counterpart after the three transforms is $(u*v)/S^2$, so after the first scale it is $w=(u*v)/S$, the exact array that $\widetilde w$ approximates.

relations.quote: [Parameter and prime-length choice](parameter-choice.md) fixes the sizes: $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ fractional bits for every stored value, distinct odd primes $s_i$ with product $S$, and powers of two $t_i$ just above $s_i$ with product $T$.

Their product polynomial has degree below $S$, so the product is reduced to a cyclic convolution modulo $x^S-1$ of digit arrays with integer coefficients below $2^{3b}$, by [Multiplication as radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-reduction.md).
The [Chinese-remainder address map](crt-map.md) $\Phi$ rewrites a length-$S$ coefficient sequence as an array with one cyclic axis of each length $s_i$ and preserves convolution.

Here $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)=f*g/T$ is normalized cyclic convolution, computed through the [Phase twist](phase-twist.md) and [Convolution from the retained transform layout](ring-convolution.md).
